title: Endpoints of a listed edge are reachable
statement: Let $\mathit{edges}$ be a list of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, and let $e$ be a weighted edge belonging to $\mathit{edges}$. Then the endpoints $u$ and $v$ of $e$ satisfy $\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}\,u\,v$; that is, they are connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}$.
hypotheses_covered: edges is a list of weighted edges on n vertices
e is an edge belonging to edges
replaced:
If $e \in \mathit{edges}$ then $\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}\,e.u\,e.v$; that is,
the two endpoints of any listed edge are immediately reachable from each other.
